newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico manufacturing employment rose in July.
newsitem.headline: Mexico manufacturing employment rose in July.

text.p: Manufacturing employment rose 3.8 percent in July, the fourth straight month of gains in the sector, the government said Sunday.

"In July of this year the occupied personnel in the manufacturing industry increased 3.8 percent compared to the same month of the previous year," the government statistics institute INEGEI said in a statement.
The report also said man-hours in the manufacturing industry rose 7.7 percent in July.
Seven of nine divisions in the country's manufacturing sector showed increases in employment in July over the year-ago period, it said.
The strongest growth came in textiles, clothing and leather goods, up 10.8 percent; metal products, machinery and equipment, up 9.1 percent, and basic metals, where employment rose 8.3 percent.
Employment in the wood and wood products industry rose 3.8 percent and chemicals, petroleum derivatives and plastics was up 2.5 percent.
Food, beverages and tobacco had a scant 0.5 percent increase. Other manufacturing employment rose 9.7 percent.
In contrast, employment fell by 1.5 percent in non-metalic mining and fell by 1.1 percent in paper, paper products, printing and publishing in July of this year compared to the same month last year.
